speaker: Leonard
text: You're making eggs for breakfast? Huh. 'Cause it looks a lot like breakfast.

speaker: Sheldon
text: This isn't breakfast, it's an experiment. I finally have time to test my hypothesis about the separation of the water molecules from the egg proteins and its impact vis-a-vis taste.

speaker: Leonard
text: Sounds yummy. I look forward to your work with bacon.

speaker: Leonard
text: You know, I'm sure if you just apologized to Gablehouser, he would give you your job back.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Why do I want my job back? I've spent the past three and a half years staring at greaseboards full of equations. Before that, I spent four years working on my thesis. Before that, I was in college, and before that, I was in the fifth grade.

speaker: Sheldon
text: This is my first day off in decades, and I am going to savor it.

speaker: Leonard
text: Okay. I'll let you get back to fixing your eggs.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I'm not just fixing my eggs, I'm fixing everyone's eggs.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Oh, well, this would be one of those circumstances that people unfamiliar with the law of large numbers would call a coincidence. I need eggs. Four dozen should suffice. Yes, and evenly distributed amongst brown, white, free range, large, extra large, and jumbo. Never mind, you won't get it right. I'd better come with you.

speaker: Penny
text: Hi, hey, I'm running out to the market. Do you guys need anything? I'm sorry?
